title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 4 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.

sections.title: QUESTION 1: Essay Writing: Narrative, Descriptive and Argumentative

questions.prompt: How long should a Grade 10 HL essay usually be?
Which essay type relies most on sensory details?
What is the sentence that states the main idea of a paragraph called?
In a narrative, you should start a new paragraph when a new character speaks.
Match each stage of the writing process to its activity.
Why should an argumentative essay mention and rebut a counter-argument?
questions.memo:
✓ It shows the writer has considered other views (1)
✓ and strengthens the argument by showing why the opposing view is weaker (1)

questions.prompt: Plan an argumentative essay on 'School uniforms should be abolished': state your stance and give TWO reasons.
questions.memo:
✓ Clear stance (1)
✓✓ Two relevant, distinct reasons (2)

questions.prompt: The main purpose of a literary essay is to:
options: argue a position about the text and prove it with evidence
list all the figures of speech in the text

questions.prompt: What is the one-sentence statement of your argument in the introduction called?
Events in a literary text are usually discussed in the past tense.
questions.explanation: Use the present tense: 'Romeo kills Tybalt'.

questions.prompt: A conclusion should restate the thesis in new words rather than introduce a new main point.
A topic says 'Critically discuss'. What does this ask you to do?
options: Weigh up different views and reach a reasoned conclusion
Give your personal opinion without evidence

questions.prompt: Match each part of a PEEL paragraph to its purpose.

pairs.right: Makes one clear claim linked to the thesis
A quotation or reference from the text
Shows how the evidence proves the claim

questions.prompt: Unpack this topic and write a thesis statement: 'The adults in Romeo and Juliet are more to blame for the tragedy than the young lovers.' Discuss.
questions.memo:
✓ identifies key words: adults, more to blame, young lovers, discuss (1)
✓ takes a clear position (agree / disagree / partly) (1)
✓ names at least two adults or examples, e.g. the feuding parents, Capulet forcing the marriage to Paris, the Friar's risky plan, the Nurse's advice (1)
✓ thesis is one clear arguable sentence that answers the topic (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 3: Drama: Elements and Techniques
sections.instructions: Read the text below, then answer the questions.

context.title: Extract: Act 2, Scene 2 (the balcony scene; public domain)
context.text:
JULIET: O Romeo, Romeo! wherefore art thou Romeo?
Deny thy father and refuse thy name;
Or, if thou wilt not, be but sworn my love,
And I'll no longer be a Capulet.

ROMEO [Aside]: Shall I hear more, or shall I speak at this?

JULIET: 'Tis but thy name that is my enemy;
Thou art thyself, though not a Montague.
…
What's in a name? that which we call a rose
By any other name would smell as sweet.

questions.prompt: In which city is Romeo and Juliet set?
In 'wherefore art thou Romeo?', 'wherefore' means…

An aside is heard by the audience but not by other characters on stage.

Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: The audience knows more than a character

questions.prompt: How does the Prologue create dramatic irony throughout the play?
questions.memo:
✓ It tells the audience the lovers will die (1)
✓ so the audience watches their hopeful plans knowing they will end in tragedy (1)

questions.prompt: Suggest a fatal flaw shared by Romeo and Juliet, and explain it.
questions.memo:
✓ Impulsiveness/haste (1)
✓ e.g. they marry within a day of meeting, and act rashly at the end (1)
